transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you that made you decide to come here today?

I guess I came in because... I don't know, nothing really feels like mine anymore. I used to get excited about things, you know? Checking out the new murals around the neighborhood, going for runs, shooting some basketball. Even just making a really good drink. I'm a bartender. But lately, I just stand there behind the bar like I don't care about any of it. 

It’s a shame, really, because we have this beautiful old mahogany bar top at work. Real thick wood, probably from the twenties or thirties. You just don't see craftsmanship like that anymore. Everything now is cheap particle board, like that stuff from Ikea. I tried putting together a bookshelf from there a couple of years ago and the screws stripped out immediately. Just cheap metal. It makes you wonder where they even source that stuff, probably some factory overseas where they don't have any quality control. My buddy Dave, he works in shipping, and he says the containers are just sitting at the port for months sometimes... wait, what did you ask me?
How long have you been feeling this way, like you don’t care about things anymore?

It’s been... I’d say about two months now. Yeah, right around two months. That’s when the bar got bought out, and just like that, everything I had been working toward got changed. 

They came in and ripped out the old taps. Put in these new digital pouring systems. I can't stand them. You have to use a touchscreen for everything now, and you can never get those screens clean. People are always poking at them with greasy fingers after eating the new menu items. They got rid of our classic pub food and brought in all this... artisanal flatbread stuff. Flatbread is just a fancy word for a skinny pizza, if you ask me. My buddy Dave—the shipping guy—he ordered one the other day and it looked like a giant cracker with some arugula thrown on it. Arugula is too bitter anyway. I tried growing it in my window box once, but the aphids got to it almost immediately. Nasty little bugs, they just swarm the leaves and suck the life right out of the plant, no matter what kind of pesticide you spray on them. I even tried that organic neem oil stuff, but it smells terrible, like rancid garlic and peanuts... 

Sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right. Two months. Yeah, about two months of just feeling like none of it matters anymore.
Have you had days where you felt down or hopeless almost every day, not just a lack of interest in things, and if so, how long have those feelings lasted?

Down? Yeah, I guess you could say that. It's just... everything feels heavy, you know? Like I'm dragging myself through mud every single day. Hopeless, too. I don't see how it gets any better. I mean, look at the world. Look at what they did to my bar. It's just a symptom of a larger problem. Everything is getting corporatized and sterilized. 

It reminds me of when my neighborhood got gentrified. I've lived in the same apartment for fifteen years. Used to be you knew everybody on the block. Old Mrs. Higgins at the corner store, she always saved me the Sunday paper. Now it's a boutique pet bakery. A bakery for dogs! Can you believe that? People are spending ten dollars on a cupcake for a golden retriever while there are folks sleeping on the grates outside. It's sick. I saw this one guy walking his labradoodle—which isn't even a real breed, it's just a mutt they charge two grand for—and he had the dog in a little sweater. A sweater! Dogs have fur for a reason. It's evolution. Charles Darwin figured that out a long time ago. I read a book about him once, fascinating guy. He went to the Galapagos Islands and studied finches... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, feeling down. Yeah. I don't know exactly how long. It's all just sort of blurred together lately. I just know I don't feel right.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or have lost energy almost every day?

Tired? Yeah, all the time. It's like I have no gas in the tank anymore. By the time I carry a couple cases of liquor from the back or just set up the well for the shift, my body feels like I've already worked a double. And that's even if I barely did anything that day. 

It's ridiculous because I used to be able to sling drinks for ten hours straight and still go out after. Now, just lifting those boxes... and they changed the boxes, too. The new distributors use this flimsy cardboard that tears if you look at it wrong. The other day, the bottom fell out of a case of vodka and shattered three bottles all over the floor. The smell was overpowering. Reminded me of this time I had to clean up after a frat party back in the nineties. Those kids used to drink this awful grain alcohol punch out of plastic trash cans. Trash cans! You don't even know what chemicals are leaching into the alcohol from the plastic. Plastic is everywhere now. It's in the ocean, it's in the fish. I watched a documentary about microplastics and how they're finding it in people's blood now. It's terrifying to think about what we're doing to ourselves without even realizing it. They say you should only use glass or stainless steel, but try telling that to management when they're trying to cut costs... 

Sorry, what was the question? Oh, energy. Yeah. I just feel totally drained, every single day.
Have you had days where you felt depressed most of the day, not just a little down, and if so, how many days in a row has this happened?

Depressed most of the day? I guess so, yeah. It’s definitely more than just feeling a little down. But how many days in a row? I really couldn't tell you. I’ve completely lost track of the days lately. 

It doesn't help that they changed how we do the schedule at work. Used to be a paper calendar pinned to the corkboard right by the walk-in cooler. You just looked at it. Simple. Now Kevin—he’s the new floor manager, kid’s barely twenty-four, rides this ridiculous electric scooter to work—he put everything on this smartphone app. I don't want to check an app to see if I'm working a Tuesday day shift. And the thing sends these notifications at all hours. It beeped at me at 3 AM the other night. I had to figure out how to silence the phone, which took forever because they hide the settings menus on these new ones. My first cell phone was a Nokia. Built like an absolute brick. You could drop it off a roof and it would still make calls, and the battery lasted a week. Now you have to plug these glass rectangles into the wall twice a day. And the charger cords always fray right at the neck, you know? They make them cheap on purpose so you have to go buy a new one for twenty bucks every few months. It's a total racket...

Uh, sorry. My brain is just... fuzzy. What did you ask me about the days? I really don't know how many it's been in a row. It just feels like one long, bad day at this point.
Have you had days where you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks or more in a row?

Two weeks? Yeah, longer than that. It's been going on for about two months now. Right around the time the bar got bought out. They brought in all this new management and just completely gutted the place. Everything I'd been working toward, the whole vibe we built over a decade, just erased overnight. 

They even got rid of the old mahogany bar top. Can you believe that? Real, solid mahogany. They replaced it with this cheap, poured concrete nonsense because it looks "industrial." Industrial! It's a bar, not a factory floor. Concrete is terrible for glassware, too. You set a pint glass down a little too hard and it shatters. And the noise! It echoes off the concrete. Used to be you could have a quiet conversation in the corner, maybe listen to the jukebox. We had a great jukebox. Real 45s. I used to stock it myself, put some Sam Cooke in there, a little Otis Redding. Now they just plug an iPad into the sound system and play this thumping electronic garbage that gives you a headache after ten minutes. It's all bass, no melody. Music used to have melody, you know? You could hum along to it. I tried explaining that to Kevin, the kid with the scooter, but he just looked at me like I was speaking a foreign language. He probably doesn't even know who Sam Cooke is. It's a tragedy, really, the way history just gets forgotten...

Wait, what did you ask me? Two weeks? Right, yeah. It's been about two months of this. Ever since the buyout.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Weight? Yeah, I've definitely lost some. Appetite is just... gone. Most days I completely forget to eat until my hands start shaking while I'm trying to pour a drink behind the bar. Then, after closing, I might try to grab a few bites of something cold from the back, but I just end up feeling sick even looking at it. 

The food they have back there now is just sad anyway. They got rid of the old kitchen staff when the buyout happened. We used to have this guy, Hector, who made the most incredible slow-roasted pork sandwiches. He'd marinate that pork for two days in this citrus garlic mojo. The smell would drift out into the bar around 4 PM and everyone's mouth would start watering. Now? Now it's all frozen appetizers they just drop in the deep fryer. Mozzarella sticks, jalapeño poppers, those little mac and cheese bites that taste like salty cardboard. And the grease they use... I swear they don't change the fryer oil nearly enough. It gets this dark, murky color and everything that comes out of it tastes like burnt fish, even if it's a french fry. I read an article once about how reused frying oil breaks down into these toxic compounds that mess with your liver. It's basically poison. But corporate doesn't care about that, they just care about the profit margin on a six-dollar plate of frozen cheese... 

Sorry, I'm rambling again. What were we talking about? Oh, right, eating. Yeah, I just don't eat much anymore. Makes me sick to think about it.
Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual, or maybe been more restless or fidgety lately—like you can't sit still?

Moving slowly? I don't... I mean, I haven't really noticed moving slower or faster. Or being fidgety. I'm just... existing, I guess. 

Though, speaking of moving, they did rearrange the entire back room where we keep the liquor stock. It used to be alphabetical by type. Vodka, then whiskey, then whatever. Made sense. Now they have it organized by "flavor profile" or some nonsense. You have to walk all the way to the back left corner just to find the well tequila, and then all the way to the front right for the top shelf stuff. It's a nightmare when it's busy. Not that it gets busy anymore. The regulars all left when they took out the mahogany bar. 

There was this one guy, Stan. Plumber. Came in every Tuesday and Thursday right at 5:15. Ordered a boilermaker and read the sports section. Didn't want to talk, just wanted a quiet place to sit after being elbow-deep in other people's pipes all day. I respected that. You gotta respect a man who knows how to be quiet. People these days, they don't know how to just sit in silence. They always have to be looking at a screen, or taking a picture of their drink. Who takes a picture of a drink? It's liquid in a glass. It's going to look exactly the same in the picture as it does on the table. And they use the flash, right in your eyes while you're trying to count change. I swear my vision has gotten worse just from people taking pictures of their stupid neon cocktails...

Anyway, what was it? Fidgety? No, I don't think so. I just don't have the energy for much of anything.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you're not worth much lately?

Yeah, I guess I do feel pretty awful about things. I keep thinking about how I let down the younger bartenders. And those local artists, too. I promised them we'd always have space on the back wall for their stuff, you know? Give them a little exposure. 

But speaking of the back wall, they painted it this sterile, hospital white. It used to be this warm, exposed brick. Do you know how much people pay for exposed brick these days? And they just slapped two coats of cheap white latex right over it. I told the contractor, I said, "You're ruining the integrity of the building," but he didn't care. He was just some guy from out of state. Didn't even have his own tools. He borrowed my hammer and never gave it back. A good Estwing hammer, too, with the stacked leather grip. My dad gave me that hammer when I first moved out. Said a man always needs a reliable hammer. You can't trust these new ones with the fiberglass handles, they vibrate right up your arm and ruin your elbow. My buddy Dave got tennis elbow so bad from swinging one of those fiberglass things he had to wear a brace for a year. He couldn't even turn a doorknob without wincing... 

Wait, what was I saying? Right, the artists. And the young kids behind the bar. I told them I'd look out for them, teach them the real trade. And now they're stuck pouring neon slushies. I wrecked their shot. Honestly, it feels like I deserve whatever happens to me now for letting it all fall apart. I'm just useless to them.
Before this current period of feeling depressed, have you ever had another episode where you felt this way for at least two weeks?

Before this? I don't... I don't think so. I've never felt like this before. It's like everything just stopped mattering all at once. 

Kind of like when they decided to stop carrying the local draft beers. We used to have this incredible stout from a microbrewery down in the valley. The guy who ran it, Mike, he'd deliver the kegs himself in this beat-up old Chevy truck. Had this dog, a golden retriever mix named Barley, who rode shotgun. Barley would always hop out and sniff around the alley while Mike unloaded. Good dog. Never barked, just wanted his ears scratched. I used to keep a box of milk bones under the counter just for him. You know, they say dogs can sense when a person is a good person. Barley always liked me. But then corporate came in and said we could only stock their approved national brands. Said the margins were better on the mass-produced stuff. So they told Mike not to come back. Just like that. After five years of doing business. I haven't seen Barley since. It's a shame, really. Dogs don't understand things like corporate buyouts and profit margins. They just know when their routine gets messed up. Just like people, I guess. We all need our routines. 

But no, to answer your question... I haven't ever had a time like this before. Not for two weeks, not for two days. This is all new. And it's just... it's terrible.

We used to have this guy, Hector, who made the most incredible slow-roasted pork sandwiches. He'd marinate that pork for two days in this citrus garlic mojo. The smell would drift out into the bar around 4 PM and everyone's mouth would start watering. Now? Now it's all frozen appetizers they just drop in the deep fryer. Mozzarella sticks, jalapeño poppers, those little mac and cheese bites that taste like salty cardboard. And the grease they use... I swear they don't change the fryer oil nearly enough. It gets this dark, murky color and everything that comes out of it tastes like burnt fish, even if it's a french fry. I read an article once about how reused frying oil breaks down into these toxic compounds that mess with your liver. It's basically poison. But corporate doesn't care about that, they just care about the profit margin on a six-dollar plate of frozen cheese... 

Sorry, I'm rambling again. What were we talking about? Oh, right, eating. Yeah, I just don't eat much anymore. Makes me sick to think about it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced psychomotor agitation or retardation, which would support a diagnosis of major depressive disorder with melancholic features (F32.2 or F33.2).
doctor.question: Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual, or maybe been more restless or fidgety lately—like you can't sit still?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about psychomotor agitation or retardation (moving slowly or being restless/fidgety), which is not included in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Moving slowly? I don't... I mean, I haven't really noticed moving slower or faster. Or being fidgety. I'm just... existing, I guess. 

Though, speaking of moving, they did rearrange the entire back room where we keep the liquor stock. It used to be alphabetical by type. Vodka, then whiskey, then whatever. Made sense. Now they have it organized by "flavor profile" or some nonsense. You have to walk all the way to the back left corner just to find the well tequila, and then all the way to the front right for the top shelf stuff. It's a nightmare when it's busy. Not that it gets busy anymore. The regulars all left when they took out the mahogany bar. 

There was this one guy, Stan. Plumber. Came in every Tuesday and Thursday right at 5:15. Ordered a boilermaker and read the sports section. Didn't want to talk, just wanted a quiet place to sit after being elbow-deep in other people's pipes all day. I respected that. You gotta respect a man who knows how to be quiet. People these days, they don't know how to just sit in silence. They always have to be looking at a screen, or taking a picture of their drink. Who takes a picture of a drink? It's liquid in a glass. It's going to look exactly the same in the picture as it does on the table. And they use the flash, right in your eyes while you're trying to count change. I swear my vision has gotten worse just from people taking pictures of their stupid neon cocktails...

Anyway, what was it? Fidgety? No, I don't think so. I just don't have the energy for much of anything.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, which is a key differentiator between F32.2 and F33.2.
doctor.question: Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you're not worth much lately?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep thinking I let down the younger bartenders and the artists I promised space to, and it feels like I deserve whatever happens to me for wrecking their shot.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of guilt, blaming oneself, or feeling worthless, which directly corresponds to the Worthlessness_Guilt symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I guess I do feel pretty awful about things. I keep thinking about how I let down the younger bartenders. And those local artists, too. I promised them we'd always have space on the back wall for their stuff, you know? Give them a little exposure. 

But speaking of the back wall, they painted it this sterile, hospital white. It used to be this warm, exposed brick. Do you know how much people pay for exposed brick these days? And they just slapped two coats of cheap white latex right over it. I told the contractor, I said, "You're ruining the integrity of the building," but he didn't care. He was just some guy from out of state. Didn't even have his own tools. He borrowed my hammer and never gave it back. A good Estwing hammer, too, with the stacked leather grip. My dad gave me that hammer when I first moved out. Said a man always needs a reliable hammer. You can't trust these new ones with the fiberglass handles, they vibrate right up your arm and ruin your elbow. My buddy Dave got tennis elbow so bad from swinging one of those fiberglass things he had to wear a brace for a year. He couldn't even turn a doorknob without wincing... 

Wait, what was I saying? Right, the artists. And the young kids behind the bar. I told them I'd look out for them, teach them the real trade. And now they're stuck pouring neon slushies. I wrecked their shot. Honestly, it feels like I deserve whatever happens to me now for letting it all fall apart. I'm just useless to them.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had recurrent episodes of major depression, which would support a diagnosis of F33.2 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder, Current Episode Severe Without Psychotic Symptoms) over F32.2 (Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, Severe Without Psychotic Symptoms).
doctor.question: Before this current period of feeling depressed, have you ever had another episode where you felt this way for at least two weeks?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a history of past depressive episodes, which is not covered by any specific item in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Before this? I don't... I don't think so. I've never felt like this before. It's like everything just stopped mattering all at once. 

Kind of like when they decided to stop carrying the local draft beers. We used to have this incredible stout from a microbrewery down in the valley. The guy who ran it, Mike, he'd deliver the kegs himself in this beat-up old Chevy truck. Had this dog, a golden retriever mix named Barley, who rode shotgun. Barley would always hop out and sniff around the alley while Mike unloaded. Good dog. Never barked, just wanted his ears scratched. I used to keep a box of milk bones under the counter just for him. You know, they say dogs can sense when a person is a good person. Barley always liked me. But then corporate came in and said we could only stock their approved national brands. Said the margins were better on the mass-produced stuff. So they told Mike not to come back. Just like that. After five years of doing business. I haven't seen Barley since. It's a shame, really. Dogs don't understand things like corporate buyouts and profit margins. They just know when their routine gets messed up. Just like people, I guess. We all need our routines. 

But no, to answer your question... I haven't ever had a time like this before. Not for two weeks, not for two days. This is all new. And it's just... it's terrible.
